options.region: No WorkOS region selected; storage destinations not verified
options.configuration: Third-party org-bound M2M; client_credentials/client_secret_post; environment audience; scoped API access

conditions: Limit this proposal to Connect bearer JWTs for an application-owned API. Validate the selected HTTPS AuthKit issuer, trusted environment /oauth2/jwks, signature, allowed algorithm, expiry and environment client ID audience. That audience is not the requesting M2M client ID or a per-application resource parameter; live issuer/key/algorithm acceptance remains unverified.

Require the machine sub and client_id to identify the registered application, its expected org_id and granted scopes before checking application-owned resource permissions. Reject missing, unknown or foreign organization/resource context. A signed org_id, decoded JWT or successful token exchange does not establish tenant isolation, human membership or administrative authority.

The claims guide gives M2M an environment client ID audience, no sid and no JWT templates/custom claims. Do not import user-token resource indicators, role-based permissions, consent or primary AuthKit session-token semantics. Granted scopes are not human permissions. Claims source: https://workos.com/docs/authkit/connect/token-claims.

Optional online validation needs a separately reviewed introspection credential policy and fail-closed transport handling. The reference example uses /oauth2/introspection but its typed endpoint heading says /oauth2/token; preserve this discrepancy before source approval. Caller/cross-client authorization and response freshness are untested. Source: https://workos.com/docs/reference/workos-connect/introspection.

The M2M token reference marks org_id optional in its typed JWT fields although the M2M guide requires an organization and its example includes org_id. Preserve that discrepancy; this API scope requires the expected organization. Reconcile scope/audience claims and actual responses before approval. Source: https://workos.com/docs/reference/workos-connect/token.

Secret rotation, scope changes, application removal, cached-token expiry and service offboarding require independent enforcement tests. Do not promise immediate rejection of already-issued JWTs or copy an example lifetime as a deployment guarantee. No API validation, introspection, revocation or resource isolation was tested; the evaluator stays synthetic.

evidence.summary: The Connect claims guide separates M2M environment audience, machine identity, organization and scopes from user tokens. OPTIONAL is a conditional API-token proposal, not verified enforcement, tenant isolation, live entitlement or reviewed evidence.

conditions: Select a third-party Connect application with application_type m2m and one explicit customer/partner organization. The M2M guide permits only third-party applications; this is not a first-party background-service or delegated-user configuration. Human login, organization switching and multiple user memberships are not inherited.

POST grant_type=client_credentials with the application's client_id/client_secret in an HTTPS form body to the selected AuthKit domain /oauth2/token; select client_secret_post only. Keep secrets on a trusted backend, outside browser/mobile bundles, URLs and logs. A WorkOS management API key is not this application secret. Basic, private_key_jwt and mTLS are outside scope. Source: https://workos.com/docs/reference/workos-connect/token.

Assign least-privilege application scopes and request an explicit subset through the optional scope parameter. Verify the returned grant rather than trusting the request; exact narrowing/default behavior is untested. Configure the organization and scopes explicitly even where the common create schema marks them optional. Application reference: https://workos.com/docs/reference/workos-connect/applications.

Use the access_token as Bearer within its validated expiry, then perform another client_credentials exchange when needed. This selected grant does not use ID Tokens, refresh tokens, end-user sessions or browser redirects. The claims guide fixes the M2M audience to the environment client ID, not a configurable per-application custom API audience.

The OpenID discovery example includes client_credentials while the OAuth authorization-server example omits it; preserve this discrepancy and do not treat examples as observed runtime metadata or complete grant support. Source: https://workos.com/docs/reference/workos-connect/metadata. Cloud sources are mutable and dated, not release-pinned.

Staging is testing-only, not customer-facing production; environments have separate keys, organizations and users. Free staging does not verify production M2M entitlement, quotas, billing or future zero-cost operation. Sources: https://workos.com/docs/authkit/environments and https://workos.com/pricing. No account, application, organization, credentials, subscription or live calls were created; no Directory Sync, SSO, residency or human controls are inherited.

evidence.summary: The M2M guide describes third-party, organization-bound Connect applications using client credentials to obtain access tokens. SUPPORTED is a staging documentation proposal with separate credential, scope, audience, resource-authorization and production-cost prerequisites.
